newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Nova Hut IFC credit price LIBOR +162.5 bps.
newsitem.headline: Nova Hut IFC credit price LIBOR +162.5 bps.

text.p: An International Finance Corporation (IFC) 12-year, $75 million credit facility for Czech steel mill Nova Hut a.s. is priced at 162.5 basis points above LIBOR, a senior official involved in arranging the credit told Reuters.
The official added that a 10-year, $175 million syndicated loan obtained at the same time by the Czech firm was priced at LIBOR +137.5 basis points.
The official, who asked not to be named, added both credits are at a fixed rate.

Earlier on Friday, Nova Hut signed deals with the IFC and a syndicate of 17 banks for the credits, part of which will be used to help finance the constrction of a hot-rolled coil mill, the construction of which is being managed by U.S.-based ICF Kaiser International.

The total $650 million project is to be completed by the year 2000, and will allow Nova hut to compete internationally as one of the low-cost steel producers of flat rather than long steel products which it has traditionally produced.
The largest participant in the syndicate was Deutsche Bank, and the IFC said eight Japanese banks provided some 40 percent of the syndicated loan financing, the IFC statement said.
The syndicate also includes banks from Austria, South Korea, the U.S., and Belgium.
